title: Calibration Frontier of Gaussian-Prepivoted Randomization Tests under Stringent Rerandomization
banked_reason: D0.5.G: meets_floor=false; normalized tier=incremental; paper_score_ceiling=6.4 < field ceiling=7.4; no same-substrate repair remains.
gap_reasons: The note proves a matched reference-modulus rate only on the logarithmically truncated coarse/fine interval, while the signed modulus has merely a lower bound of order (nq²)^-1 beyond the fixed-coefficient elbow; its available upper bound does not determine the growing-shell rate.

Resolve the signed-frontier question by proving Omega_n^+(q) <= C/(nq²) uniformly on J_n when sqrt(n)q diverges, or by constructing a legal population attaining a strictly larger rate and matching that rate from above.

Existing Berry--Esseen, concentration, and coarse/fine machinery cannot control diagonal ranks, randomized ties, accepted-shell score multiplicities, or recomputed-plugin perturbations uniformly under small variance; either route needs genuinely new rank-sensitive/accepted-shell/local-lattice substrate or a new extremal construction.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved uniform exact-mass upper envelopes, explicit coarse/fine populations with Delta_ref = Theta(m^-1) and Delta_plus = Theta(m^-2), continuous lower frontiers on J_n, a matched reference rate above the logarithmic cutoff, and fixed-coefficient elbow results. Nine D0 rounds exhausted the existing construction. The field claim failed because no class-uniform matching upper bound for the signed modulus was obtained; closing it requires new rank-sensitive accepted-shell/local-lattice machinery or a new extremal witness.
tldr: For the fixed Gaussian-prepivoted randomization test over the frozen bounded scalar-covariate finite-population class, the note establishes provable partial calibration boundaries: generic finite-mass and sharper reference-only upper bounds, legal coarse/fine populations with \(\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}=\Theta(m^{-1})\) and \(\Delta_+=\Theta(m^{-2})\), continuous lower frontiers on \(\mathcal J_n\), matching reference control above the logarithmic cutoff, and classification of every supported fixed-coefficient elbow window. Exact finite maps evaluate both losses once the complete outcome-sensitive score table is supplied, but that table is not observable from \((x,a,\mathcal A_a(P))\) before treatment; even the entire labeled accepted set is insufficient, and geometry-fiber suprema remain unevaluated variational characterizations. The population class requires armwise residual nondegeneracy but no residual upper assumption; bounded outcomes provide the needed upper scale. An exact-full-accepted-set conditional selector converts separately proved deterministic envelopes into a tolerance guarantee, while a bottom return has no weak-null implication. Exact randomized complete-accepted-set ranks retain finite-sample sharp-null exactness. No numerical envelope constants, finite accepted-pool guarantee, or Monte Carlo error control is supplied.
gap: Existing Gaussian prepivoting theory gives qualitative weak-null asymptotic protection and exact sharp-null inference, while diminishing-acceptance rerandomization theory controls the conditional estimator law. Neither identifies the signed rejection error or the observed-assignment-specific recomputed reference CDF as a joint function of finite population size and exact acceptance mass.
fill: The project will classify the two intrinsic moduli, prove or kill the candidate squared signed rate through an \(o(m^{-2})\) transfer, establish a uniform upper theory that handles cancellation and atoms, and convert effective constants plus accepted-set geometry into a threshold certificate with a sharp-null-exact fallback.
